title: Months Taken Off a Reinstated Plan According to Its Breakdown — Benefit Overpayment Accounts
content:
Months are taken off the reinstatement months of a reinstated Benefit Overpayment Accounts repayment plan according to when the plan broke down, dated by its most recent returned installment: the most recent return entry booked on the overpayment. The breakdown is measured in whole months from the plan's first installment due date to that return's booking date.

| Whole months from the first installment due date to the most recent return | Months taken off the reinstatement months |
|---|---|
| Fewer than 6 (the early-breakdown months) | The reinstated plan keeps the end the defaulted plan was set to have, so the whole months elapsed from the first installment due date to the handling date are taken off |
| At least 6 but fewer than 12 (the mid-breakdown months) | Only the whole months from that return to the handling date are taken off |
| 12 or more, or no installment has been returned | Nothing is taken off; the reinstatement months run afresh from the reinstatement |

## Interpretive note

The three rows reflect how much of the defaulted plan's schedule the reinstated plan keeps. A plan that broke down early keeps its original end; a plan that broke down later loses only the months that have run since the breakdown; a plan that ran for a year or more before breaking down starts its reinstatement months afresh.

## Hypothetical cases

| First installment due | Most recent return booked | Months to the return | Handling date | Months taken off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15 January | 20 April | 3 | 25 July | 6 (15 January to 25 July) |
| 15 January | 1 September | 7 | 10 November | 2 (1 September to 10 November) |
| 15 January of the previous year | 20 February | 13 | 1 May | None |
